title: Konsult Flows
subtitle: A small consulting bookkeeping app built on Act 2.0: clients, invoices, the year's Book and recurring expenses, where every invoice action books its money on the Book in the same commit.

nodes.label: CreateInvoice
preconditions: Period already has an active invoice — void it first to start a new draft
nodes.schema:
clientId: string
month: string
rate: number
paymentTermsDays?: number
entries: Record<string, {
  hours: number ≥ 0.25, ≤ 16
  description: string ≥ 5 chars
  drove?: boolean
}>
expenses?: Record<string, {
  category: "Travel" | "Meals" | "Lodging" | "Other"
  description: string ≥ 3 chars
  amount: number > 0
  date: string
  receiptId?: string
}>
clientName?: string
clientAddress?: string
clientEmail?: string
commuteMiles?: number
paymentInstructions?: string
nodes.description: Starts a draft from the day entries and billed expenses, snapshotting the client's name, address, commute and terms so the invoice never drifts. Throws when there is nothing to bill, a billed expense has no receipt, or hours are billed with no rate.

nodes.label: AdjustInvoice
preconditions: Invoice must be in draft status
nodes.schema:
rate?: number
notes?: string
entries?: Record<string, {
  hours: number ≥ 0.25, ≤ 16
  description: string ≥ 5 chars
  drove?: boolean
} | null>
expenses?: Record<string, {
  category: "Travel" | "Meals" | "Lodging" | "Other"
  description: string ≥ 3 chars
  amount: number > 0
  date: string
  receiptId?: string
} | null>
nodes.description: The caller sends the full intended entries and expenses; the emit handler diffs them against the draft so the event carries only what changed. Refuses a change that changes nothing.

nodes.label: SendInvoice
preconditions: Invoice must be in draft status
nodes.schema: dueDate?: date
nodes.description: Issues the invoice (issue date today, due date from the terms) and, in the same commit, books its commute mileage and billed expenses on the period year's Book. Loads `book-{year}` and, for invoices created before the commute snapshot, reads the live Client. maxRetries 2.

nodes.label: DiscardDraft
preconditions: Only an unsent draft can be discarded
nodes.schema: reason: string
nodes.description: Throws away a draft that was never issued. Nothing was booked, so it touches no Book.

nodes.label: VoidInvoice
preconditions: Only an issued invoice with no payments can be voided
nodes.schema: reason: string
nodes.description: Reverses an issued, unpaid invoice and un-books its reimbursements on the same Book in the same commit, carrying the void's reason. maxRetries 2.

nodes.label: RecordPayment
nodes.schema:
paidDate: string
paidAmount: number
paymentMethod?: string
reference: string ≥ 1 chars
nodes.description: Settles the invoice in full and books the income on the Book of the paid date's year (cash basis), in the same commit. maxRetries 2.

scenarios.title: Getting set up
scenarios.summary: The consultant fills in the business profile and the tax year, registers a client, and lets Google Maps work out the commute.

steps.say: First the **business profile**: it prints on every invoice. Settings live in one `settings` stream.
No rules to check: the profile is just recorded.
Then the **2026 tax inputs**: filing status and W-2 withholding feed the quarterly estimate.
Recorded on `taxyear-2026`.
Now a client: **Acme**, at $150 an hour, net 30.
The stream is new, so the slug is free. **ClientRegistered** lands and **clients_view** picks it up.
A second **Register Acme**, from another tab.
Refused: the stream already holds Acme.
steps.reject: A client with this slug is already registered

steps.say: **Calculate commute** asks Google Maps for the driving distance from the business to Acme.
**12.4 miles**, one way. The router saves it with UpdateClient.
The event carries only what changed.
Acme agrees to a new rate.
Again only the changed field lands.

scenarios.title: One commit, two streams
scenarios.summary: June's invoice is drafted, issued and paid. Sending it books its mileage and billed flight on book-2026 in the same commit; the payment books the income the same way.

steps.say: The year's money lives on **book-2026**, a stream of its own. Before Act 2.0, reactions copied an invoice's money onto it after the fact. Now the invoice actions **load the Book** and append to it themselves.
The consultant drafts **June for Acme**: 12 days, 4 of them driven, and a $320 flight with its receipt.
The period had no active invoice, so the draft starts. It snapshots Acme's commute and terms.
One more day turns up. The consultant saves the whole timesheet again.
The emit handler diffs it against the draft: only the **new day** goes on the event.
**Send**. SendInvoice loads its own stream and **book-2026** at v41. The invoice already carries the commute, so the Client read is skipped.

One commit, **two streams**: InvoiceSent on the invoice, and on the Book the drive days as mileage and the flight as a deductible expense. Both streams are checked at the versions loaded, then everything lands at once.
**emailInvoice** builds the PDF from the committed dates and mails it to Acme.
Acme pays by ACH on **July 28**. RecordPayment loads the Book of the **paid date's** year: cash basis.
The invoice is settled and the income is booked, in **one commit**. There is no moment where the invoice says paid and the Book doesn't know.

scenarios.title: Void and start over
scenarios.summary: July went out at the wrong rate. Voiding it un-books its expenses in the same commit; the period is re-drafted, and an unneeded draft is discarded.

steps.say: July was issued at the old rate. **Void** loads book-2026 at v47, where the invoice's $180 hotel is booked.
It's issued and unpaid, so it can be voided. The same commit **un-books** the hotel on the Book, carrying the void's reason.
A voided period can start over. A fresh draft at the right rate.
Every per-cycle field resets; the voided cycle stays in the audit trail.
A payment arrives early, against the draft.
Refused before anything is written: nothing lands on the invoice **or** the Book.
The consultant tries to void the draft instead of discarding it.
Void is for issued invoices.
steps.reject: Only an issued invoice with no payments can be voided

steps.say: The client will be billed in August instead. **Discard** the draft.
Nothing was issued, so nothing was booked and no Book is touched.

scenarios.title: A lost race, retried
scenarios.summary: An old Globex invoice, created before invoices snapshot the commute, is sent while a recurring expense lands on the same Book. The commit loses the race, reloads and lands.

steps.say: This draft predates the commute snapshot, so SendInvoice also **reads** client-globex: 9 miles. It loads book-2025 at **v88**.
Meanwhile a recurring expense landed on book-2025, which is now at v89. The Book's check fails, so **nothing lands** on either stream: ConcurrencyError.
SendInvoice has **maxRetries 2**. It runs again with fresh loads: book-2025 at v89. The client is only read, so its version isn't checked.
This time both checks pass. The invoice is sent and 4 drive days × 9 miles × 2 land on the Book.

scenarios.title: Refusals
scenarios.summary: Every way the invoice turns a request down, each before anything is written.

steps.say: A second draft for August, from a stale tab.
August already has an active invoice.
steps.reject: Period already has an active invoice — void it first to start a new draft

steps.say: The consultant hits Save without changing anything.
An adjust that changes nothing isn't a fact.
steps.reject: No changes to save — the invoice already matches what you submitted.

steps.say: Send, with a due date typed in the past. The Book is loaded at v52.
The emit handler refuses it, so neither the invoice nor the Book changes.
steps.reject: Due date cannot be before the issue date

scenarios.title: Keeping the books
scenarios.summary: The consultant records what no invoice books: expenses, trips and their corrections, a 401(k) contribution and a quarterly payment.

steps.say: A new **monitor**, $480, as equipment.
Recorded at 100% deductible; the tax estimate is recomputed on the fold.
The receipt says $450.
Only the changed field goes on the event.
A duplicate software charge gets voided.
Voided rows stay on the Book, excluded from totals.
A round trip to a client workshop, 38 miles each way.
The event stores the doubled total and snapshots this year's rate.
The detour via I-35 made it 92 miles.
One commit voids the original and books the correction, at the trip year's rate.
A trip logged twice.
Voided, and dropped from the deduction.
A $90,000 solo 401(k) contribution.
Over the year's cap, so the emit handler refuses it.
steps.reject: Combined 401(k) contributions $90,000 exceed the 2026 §415(c) limit of $70,000.

steps.say: $15,000 instead.
Within the cap and below net earnings.
The Q2 estimated payment goes out.
Last write wins per quarter.

scenarios.title: Recurring expenses
scenarios.summary: A monthly software subscription as a template: changed, paused, resumed, skipped, ended and deleted, with its months booked on the Book when the consultant confirms them.

steps.say: **Figma**, $45 a month from January.
All templates share one `recurring-expenses` stream.
The consultant **confirms the pending months**. The materializer books each one on book-2026 with a deterministic id, skipping months already there.
January lands as an ordinary expense.
The price goes up to $55.
Only the changed field.
Paused for a slow summer.
Future months stop booking.
Back on in September.
Booking resumes.
October was comped.
The materializer will skip it.
Cancelled after November.
No months book after the end.
Removed from the list. The months already booked stay on the Book.
Marked deleted, never erased.
